events.text:
## Recommendation

- Expect slow pier salmon fishing this week at all four ports. My ratings: **St. Joseph 1, South Haven 1, Grand Haven 0, Muskegon 0**.
- Go to **South Haven** pier if you pick one. It's tied with St. Joseph, but its buoy showed a sharp drop that may be upwelling.
- Use spoons, the method that caught the few pier fish reported. Fish early or late in the day, when the reports say pier catches happened.
- If you can, boats were doing better than piers (see Evidence). A pier trip is a low-odds bet.

## Why

- Every recent pier report this fall has been rated slow or below average, so I'd expect a slow week at the piers.
- Muskegon and Grand Haven had the slowest pier reports most recently, so I rated them lowest.
- South Haven's buoy showed a sharp drop, the sign of upwelling that brings salmon toward piers, so I'd expect it to be the slightly better bet.
- Past mid-October weeks with similar water temperatures also had slow pier reports, so I'd expect this week to follow that pattern.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (latest bulletin is 2025-10-09, five days old)
- Grand Haven, 2025-10-09: "Pier anglers targeting salmon found the action to be slow." Boats did better: spoons at 40–90 ft down in 80–160 ft of water.
- Grand Haven, 2025-10-01: pier "slow," with a couple of fish on glow spoons in low light.
- Muskegon, 2025-10-01: pier "also slow." Boats had a mixed result and only got a few plugs and spoons.
- Muskegon, 2025-09-17: "Pier anglers casting spoons for salmon were unsuccessful."
- South Haven, 2025-10-01: "Pier fishing was a little slow. There were a couple of salmon caught by anglers casting spoons." (Rated 1.) No pier mention in the 2025-10-09 South Haven report.
- St. Joseph, 2025-10-01: "the piers were a little slow." No pier mention in the 2025-10-09 report.
- St. Joseph, 2025-09-24: pier slow, a few fish on shrimp. Boats rated good (3) that week with fish beyond 100 ft.
- South Haven, 2025-10-09 boats: 1 (below average). St. Joseph, 2025-10-09 boats: "very inconsistent," rated 1.

**Past seasons** (general history, not current reports; weeks with buoy water near 61 °F in mid-October)
- St. Joseph pier was slow in 2022-10-05, 2023-10-04, and 2023-10-11.
- Grand Haven pier was slow in 2024-10-02.
- South Haven pier was "very inconsistent" in 2024-10-02 (rated 1).

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water in the week before today: St. Joseph 58 °F (down 4 °F), South Haven 61 °F (down 3 °F, flagged as a possible upwelling), Grand Haven and Muskegon 63 °F (down 4 °F each).
- The tool returned a backtest summary, not live data. It has no modeled pierhead temperature and no 3-day wind forecast, so I can't say what the pier water is doing now.

## Caveats

- The newest report is five days old, and the pier comments are from 2025-10-01 or earlier at most ports. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- The conditions I have are buoy readings from offshore, not pierhead water. I couldn't check the modeled pierhead temperature or wind, which matter most for pier upwelling.
- The ratings are my judgment from a small number of pier comments per port, not a DNR rating.
- The South Haven and St. Joseph ratings are close, and the difference is based on the buoy drop, not on a pier report.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin, 2025-10-09: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f6328e
- Bulletin, 2025-10-01: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f5314a
- Bulletin, 2025-09-24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f41b68
- Bulletin, 2025-09-17: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3f30d9c
- Past-season bulletins: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3754df7, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/37424d6, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b980f9, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/330b601
